headline: Adirondack Trail Permits and Olympic Venue Booking
reservation: While the Adirondack Park has no central entry fee, specific high-demand areas like the Adirondack Loj trailhead may require parking fees or advanced permits. Olympic venues and the Whiteface Memorial Highway require separate tickets; check the Olympic Authority website for current seasonal schedules.

days.title: Village Heritage and Mirror Lake

stops.name: Mirror Lake Loop
stops.detail: A paved 2.7-mile circuit providing panoramic views of the high peaks without leaving town.

stops.name: Lake Placid Olympic Museum
stops.detail: Explore the history of the 1932 and 1980 Winter Games through interactive exhibits.

days.note: Mirror Lake is electric-motor only, providing a quieter environment for morning paddling.

days.title: Mountain Summits and River Corridors

stops.name: Whiteface Veterans' Memorial Highway
stops.detail: Drive to the summit of the fifth-highest peak in NY for 360-degree Adirondack views.

stops.name: High Falls Gorge
stops.detail: Walk the bridge system to see four waterfalls along the West Branch of the Ausable River.

days.driving: Allow 60 minutes for the mountain drive; conditions vary
days.note: The highway is seasonal and closes during high winds or early snow; verify status online.

days.title: Wilderness Gateways
days.start: Suggested: 7 AM from Adirondack Loj Road

stops.name: Heart Lake
stops.detail: Enjoy a lakeside walk at the base of the High Peaks Wilderness area.

stops.name: Mount Jo
stops.detail: A steep but manageable climb for views of Mount Marcy and the MacIntyre Range.

days.note: Parking at the Loj fills very early on summer weekends; have a backup plan in Wilmington.

intel.title: High Peaks Trailheads
intel.text: Trailhead parking along Route 73 is strictly enforced; vehicles parked outside designated white lines will be ticketed. The Loj lot often fills by 7 AM in peak season.

intel.title: Mountain Shadows
intel.text: Cellular coverage is reliable in Lake Placid village but non-existent once you enter the High Peaks Wilderness. Always carry a physical map for hiking.

intel.title: Village Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and large supermarkets are concentrated on the south end of Lake Placid village. Beyond Wilmington, services become scarce in the mountain passes.

intel.title: Mud Season Constraints
intel.text: High-elevation trails are often closed in April and May to prevent erosion. Stick to paved village paths or lower valley trails during the spring thaw.

intel.title: Waterfront Rights
intel.text: Much of Lake Placid's shoreline is private; use the public launch at the north end of Mirror Lake Drive for legal access. Mirror Lake is closed to gas motors.

plan.arrival: Fly into Adirondack Regional Airport (SLK); pick up your vehicle and drive 30 minutes to Lake Placid to secure supplies before village check-in.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for village roads; winter travelers must verify the presence of snow tires or AWD for mountain passes.
plan.goldenHour: Mirror Lake Public Beach offers sunset views behind the village skyline and mountain peaks.
